title: Weekly paclitaxel with three-weekly carboplatin
context_label: Ovarian, fallopian tube and primary peritoneal cancer
schedule_label: Both day 1. Paclitaxel alone days 8 and 15.
schedule_summary: Paclitaxel and carboplatin together. Paclitaxel alone on both visits. Repeat the cycle every 21 days. The planned course is 3–6 cycles after surgery or six in advanced disease, if suitable.
purpose: The team chooses this weekly schedule to reduce recurrence risk after surgery or to treat advanced disease.
indication_text: This schedule can be used after surgery for selected high-risk early ovarian cancers, or for advanced ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer.
administration_text: Paclitaxel runs over about an hour each week. Carboplatin follows it on day 1 only. You still attend on days 8 and 15.
monitoring_summary: Report changes in walking, grip or sensation before paclitaxel.
review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.
agents.mechanism: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report numbness and tell the nurse immediately if you flush or wheeze during treatment.
visual: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
agents.mechanism: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, hearing changes or an infusion reaction.
visual: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.

common_effects.title: Hair and scalp · Paclitaxel
common_effects.text: Hair loss is likely. Ask the unit about scalp cooling or wig support before treatment.

common_effects.title: Nerves · Paclitaxel
common_effects.text: Report tingling, numb toes, poor balance or difficulty with buttons before the next dose.

common_effects.title: Nausea and vomiting · Chemotherapy
common_effects.text: Use your prescribed anti-sickness plan. Call if vomiting continues or you cannot drink.

common_effects.title: Muscles and joints · Paclitaxel
common_effects.text: Tell the team about aches that limit walking or interrupt sleep.

serious_effects.title: Infusion reaction · Infused medicines
serious_effects.text: Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, wheeze or chest tightness during treatment.

serious_effects.title: Nerves · Paclitaxel
serious_effects.text: Report tingling, numb toes, poor balance or difficulty with buttons before the next dose.

serious_effects.title: Infection or bleeding · Chemotherapy
serious_effects.text: Fever, shivering, unexplained bleeding or suddenly feeling unwell? Call the oncology team now.

serious_effects.title: Kidneys · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Tell the team if you pass much less urine or cannot keep fluids down. Kidney checks guide treatment.

serious_effects.title: Nausea and vomiting · Chemotherapy
serious_effects.text: Use your prescribed anti-sickness plan. Call if vomiting continues or you cannot drink.

serious_effects.title: Hearing · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Report new ringing in your ears or reduced hearing.

questions.q: Which visits involve paclitaxel alone, and when should you report numbness or fever?
questions.a: Talk through this with your nurse and write the answer on your appointment sheet.

questions.q: Who can I contact outside clinic hours?
questions.a: Ask the team to fill in your wallet card with local numbers.

support.title: Day 1
support.text: Your unit plans anti-sickness medicines for carboplatin and anti-allergy medicines for paclitaxel.

support.title: Days 8 and 15
support.text: The anti-allergy plan can change after the first infusion. Ask which medicines apply to today’s paclitaxel-only visit.

teachback: Which visits involve paclitaxel alone, and when should you report numbness or fever?
consent_support: Discuss the expected benefit, side effects, fertility, alternatives and symptom-directed care with the treating clinician. You may ask for more time or change your decision.
safety_note: Fever, shaking chills, unusual bleeding or sudden illness? Call the oncology unit now.
urgent_extra: Fever, shaking chills, unusual bleeding or sudden illness? Call the oncology unit now.

evidence.title: GOG-0262
evidence.interpretation: In the US randomised study, weekly paclitaxel did not significantly prolong time before cancer progression in the overall study population compared with three-weekly paclitaxel.
evidence.limitations: Bevacizumab use varied. This result does not predict which schedule will suit an individual.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before starting
cells: Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, and a kidney filtration assessment for carboplatin dosing. Nerve and hearing assessments if indicated.
Confirm which checks are booked before your first infusion.

rows.label: Every week
cells: Full blood count with differential, kidney and liver tests.
Report changes in walking, grip or sensation before paclitaxel.

monitoring_schedule.note: Scans and any tumour-marker tests follow your individual treatment plan.

sections.title: If a visit changes
sections.text: Your team will tell you if a visit moves after a delay. Do not work out a new date yourself.

sections.title: Before starting treatment
sections.text: Discuss fertility, contraception and breastfeeding with your team. Bring your current medicines and details of previous infusion reactions.
